questions.prompt: Which statement best explains the aim of Religious Education in Grade 8?
options: To connect religious teachings with responsible choices in daily life
To make learners ignore other subjects
To rank classmates by their faith
To avoid discussing values in school
questions.correctAnswer: To connect religious teachings with responsible choices in daily life
questions.explanation: Religious Education helps learners understand beliefs and apply values such as honesty, respect, service, and peace.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how Religious Education guides personal growth and responsible living.

questions.prompt: Which value is most clearly shown when a learner speaks truthfully even when it is difficult?
options: Integrity
Envy
Carelessness
Selfishness
questions.correctAnswer: Integrity
questions.explanation: Integrity means being honest and morally upright even when there is pressure to do otherwise.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify values that guide responsible conduct in school and community life.

questions.prompt: What does religious tolerance mainly require from learners in a diverse classroom?
options: Respecting people whose beliefs and practices differ from theirs
Forcing everyone to worship in the same way
Laughing at unfamiliar religious customs
Refusing to work with learners from other faiths
questions.correctAnswer: Respecting people whose beliefs and practices differ from theirs
questions.explanation: Tolerance protects dignity and allows people of different beliefs to learn and work together peacefully.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe attitudes that promote respect among people of different faiths.

questions.prompt: Which action best shows humility during a group discussion about religion?
options: Listening carefully and admitting when one needs to learn more
Interrupting others to prove superiority
Mocking beliefs that sound unfamiliar
Refusing to hear any explanation
questions.correctAnswer: Listening carefully and admitting when one needs to learn more
questions.explanation: Humility allows a learner to listen, learn, and speak respectfully without claiming to know everything.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate humble and respectful conduct when discussing religious matters.

questions.prompt: A learner finds money near the school gate and takes it to the office. Which religious value is being applied?
options: Honesty
Greed
Disobedience
Pride
questions.correctAnswer: Honesty
questions.explanation: Returning found property shows honesty because the learner respects what belongs to another person.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply religious values to everyday choices involving property and trust.

questions.prompt: Why is conscience important in moral decision making?
options: It helps a person judge right and wrong before acting
It removes the need to think about consequences
It allows any action if friends approve
It makes rules unnecessary in a community
questions.correctAnswer: It helps a person judge right and wrong before acting
questions.explanation: Conscience guides reflection before action and helps a learner choose what is morally responsible.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of conscience in making responsible decisions.

questions.prompt: Which situation best shows peer pressure that requires moral courage?
options: Friends urge a learner to cheat during a test
A teacher asks learners to revise quietly
A club invites members to plant trees
A family plans a visit to a relative
questions.correctAnswer: Friends urge a learner to cheat during a test
questions.explanation: Moral courage is needed when a learner must refuse wrongdoing despite pressure from friends.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize situations that require courage to uphold religious and moral values.

questions.prompt: A class wants to learn about different faith communities in the neighbourhood. Which method is most respectful?
options: Prepare fair questions and invite knowledgeable representatives to share
Collect rumours from social media
Visit places of worship to disturb prayers
Compare religions through insults
questions.correctAnswer: Prepare fair questions and invite knowledgeable representatives to share
questions.explanation: Respectful inquiry uses accurate sources and treats each community with dignity.
questions.learningOutcome: Use respectful inquiry to learn from different religious communities.

questions.prompt: Which question would best help a learner evaluate a difficult choice using religious values?
options: Will this choice protect truth, dignity, and responsibility?
Will this choice make me look powerful?
Will this choice hide the facts from adults?
Will this choice help me avoid every duty?
questions.correctAnswer: Will this choice protect truth, dignity, and responsibility?
questions.explanation: A values-based question tests whether a choice respects people and follows moral responsibility.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze choices using religious values such as truth, dignity, and responsibility.

questions.prompt: A Grade 8 group is creating a class values charter. Which item should be included?
options: We will speak truthfully, respect differences, and repair harm when we are wrong
We will ignore learners who disagree with us
We will copy homework whenever work is hard
We will keep quiet when someone is mistreated
questions.correctAnswer: We will speak truthfully, respect differences, and repair harm when we are wrong
questions.explanation: A good values charter names positive duties that guide daily conduct and peaceful relationships.
questions.learningOutcome: Create practical commitments that apply religious values in class life.

questions.prompt: Which sacred text is central to Christian worship and teaching?
options: The Bible
The Bhagavad Gita
The Analects
A school atlas
questions.correctAnswer: The Bible
questions.explanation: Christians use the Bible for worship, teaching, prayer, and guidance in moral living.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify sacred texts used by selected religious traditions.

questions.prompt: Which sacred text do Muslims regard as the revealed word of God?
options: The Quran
The Bible
The Vedas
The Tripitaka
questions.correctAnswer: The Quran
questions.explanation: The Quran is central to Islamic belief, worship, and guidance for daily life.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify sacred texts used by selected religious traditions.

questions.prompt: What is the Hadith in Islamic tradition?
options: Reports about the sayings and actions of Prophet Muhammad
A list of market days
A type of school uniform
A map of ancient trade routes
questions.correctAnswer: Reports about the sayings and actions of Prophet Muhammad
questions.explanation: Hadith helps Muslims understand the Prophet's example and apply Islamic teachings responsibly.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe sources of guidance used in selected religious traditions.

questions.prompt: Which Hindu text is well known for teaching about duty, devotion, and wisdom through a dialogue?
options: The Bhagavad Gita
The Gospel of Luke
The Hadith
The Psalms
questions.correctAnswer: The Bhagavad Gita
questions.explanation: The Bhagavad Gita presents teachings on duty, devotion, self-control, and spiritual understanding.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify examples of sacred writings from selected traditions.

questions.prompt: Why should learners consider context when reading a short quotation from a sacred text?
options: Context helps them understand the intended meaning more accurately
Context makes every interpretation unnecessary
Context allows them to change the text freely
Context is only useful for science lessons
questions.correctAnswer: Context helps them understand the intended meaning more accurately
questions.explanation: Reading the surrounding message and seeking guidance reduces misunderstanding and misuse of sacred texts.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why context is important when interpreting religious teachings.

questions.prompt: Which practice shows respect when handling a sacred text in class?
options: Using it carefully and returning it to a clean, safe place
Writing jokes in its pages
Throwing it across the room
Using it to cover food
questions.correctAnswer: Using it carefully and returning it to a clean, safe place
questions.explanation: Sacred texts are treated respectfully because they are important sources of faith and guidance for believers.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate respectful handling of sacred texts and religious materials.

questions.prompt: A religious story teaches that a person should forgive an offender who has repented. Which value is emphasized?
options: Reconciliation
Revenge
Dishonesty
Mockery
questions.correctAnswer: Reconciliation
questions.explanation: Reconciliation aims to restore peace and relationships after wrong has been acknowledged.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify values taught through religious stories and teachings.

questions.prompt: Which method best helps a learner compare teachings on generosity from two religions?
options: List each teaching, identify shared values, and note differences respectfully
Choose one teaching without reading the other
Ask classmates to vote on which religion is better
Copy only the longest paragraph from each text
questions.correctAnswer: List each teaching, identify shared values, and note differences respectfully
questions.explanation: Respectful comparison looks for meaning, common values, and differences without ranking or ridicule.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare moral teachings from different traditions respectfully.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion is most reasonable after studying teachings about honesty in several faith traditions?
options: Many religions encourage truthfulness as a foundation for trust
Honesty matters only when adults are watching
Religions always reject truthfulness
Truthfulness is useful only in business studies
questions.correctAnswer: Many religions encourage truthfulness as a foundation for trust
questions.explanation: Religious teachings often support honesty because truthful conduct builds trust and protects dignity.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain shared moral values found in selected religious teachings.

questions.prompt: Which response best shows careful interpretation of a religious teaching that seems difficult to understand?
options: Study the passage, ask a trusted teacher, and consider the wider teaching
Use the sentence to insult others immediately
Ignore every explanation from knowledgeable people
Change the words to fit a personal opinion
questions.correctAnswer: Study the passage, ask a trusted teacher, and consider the wider teaching
questions.explanation: Careful interpretation uses context, guidance, and reflection before applying a teaching.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze ways to interpret sacred teachings responsibly.

questions.prompt: Which project would best show learners applying a sacred teaching about compassion?
options: Organising a respectful visit and support activity for vulnerable community members
Laughing at people who need help
Collecting donations without recording them
Avoiding anyone facing difficulty
questions.correctAnswer: Organising a respectful visit and support activity for vulnerable community members
questions.explanation: Compassion becomes practical when learners plan respectful support that protects dignity and meets real needs.
questions.learningOutcome: Create practical ways of applying religious teachings on compassion.

questions.prompt: What is prayer in many religious traditions?
options: Communication with God or a spiritual reality
A method for measuring rainfall
A way of avoiding all duties
A form of school punishment
questions.correctAnswer: Communication with God or a spiritual reality
questions.explanation: Prayer is commonly understood as worshipful communication, which may include praise, thanks, confession, or request.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the meaning and purpose of prayer in religious life.

questions.prompt: Which practice is commonly used by Muslims as an act of worship performed at set times?
options: Salah
Baptism
Diwali
Meditation only
questions.correctAnswer: Salah
questions.explanation: Salah is the regular ritual prayer performed by Muslims as part of worship and obedience to God.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify selected forms of worship in different religious traditions.

questions.prompt: Which Christian practice symbolizes entry into the faith community for many Christians?
options: Baptism
Zakat
Diwali
Ahimsa
questions.correctAnswer: Baptism
questions.explanation: Baptism is a Christian rite linked with faith, cleansing, and belonging to the Christian community.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify selected rites and symbols used in religious communities.

questions.prompt: Which Hindu festival is widely associated with light overcoming darkness and good overcoming evil?
options: Diwali
Eid al-Fitr
Christmas
Pentecost
questions.correctAnswer: Diwali
questions.explanation: Diwali is a Hindu festival of lights and is often linked with hope, goodness, and renewal.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify selected religious festivals and the values they communicate.

questions.prompt: Why do many believers fast during special religious seasons?
options: To practise self-control, devotion, and compassion for others
To avoid all school responsibilities
To prove that food has no value
To make other people feel inferior
questions.correctAnswer: To practise self-control, devotion, and compassion for others
questions.explanation: Fasting can train discipline, deepen worship, and remind believers to care for people in need.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the moral and spiritual purposes of fasting in religious life.

questions.prompt: Which behaviour shows respect when visiting a mosque, church, temple, or shrine?
options: Following the expected conduct and avoiding disruption
Touching sacred items without permission
Taking photos where they are not allowed
Making jokes during worship
questions.correctAnswer: Following the expected conduct and avoiding disruption
questions.explanation: Respectful visitors observe rules, dress and behave appropriately, and protect the dignity of worshippers.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply respectful behaviour when visiting places of worship.

questions.prompt: How can worship strengthen a believer's moral life?
options: It reminds the believer of values and duties to God and other people
It removes the need to treat people fairly
It makes kindness unnecessary outside the worship place
It teaches that rules never matter
questions.correctAnswer: It reminds the believer of values and duties to God and other people
questions.explanation: Worship can renew commitment to values such as love, justice, gratitude, and service.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how worship can influence moral choices and relationships.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to interview a worship leader for a class project. Which step should come first?
options: Seek permission and prepare respectful questions
Arrive during worship and demand answers
Record private conversations secretly
Ask questions designed to embarrass the leader
questions.correctAnswer: Seek permission and prepare respectful questions
questions.explanation: Permission and respectful questions protect trust and make the learning activity appropriate.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan respectful ways to learn about worship practices from community members.

questions.prompt: Which comparison of religious festivals is most respectful and useful?
options: Compare the values taught, symbols used, and ways people prepare
Rank festivals by how much noise they make
Ignore what believers say about the festival
Mock practices that are unfamiliar
questions.correctAnswer: Compare the values taught, symbols used, and ways people prepare
questions.explanation: A useful comparison studies meaning and practice while respecting each community.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze similarities and differences in religious festivals respectfully.

questions.prompt: Which plan would best help a class observe a quiet reflection moment before a service project?
options: Agree on inclusive wording, keep it voluntary, and connect reflection to service values
Force every learner to use one prayer from one faith
Use the time to shame learners who are quiet
Cancel service unless everyone has the same belief
questions.correctAnswer: Agree on inclusive wording, keep it voluntary, and connect reflection to service values
questions.explanation: Inclusive reflection respects diversity while helping learners focus on shared values for service.
questions.learningOutcome: Create respectful reflection practices for a religiously diverse school setting.

questions.prompt: Which family practice can help pass religious values from one generation to another?
options: Sharing faith stories and discussing values at home
Avoiding all conversation with elders
Hiding family responsibilities from children
Mocking traditions during family gatherings
questions.correctAnswer: Sharing faith stories and discussing values at home
questions.explanation: Families often teach values through stories, example, worship, guidance, and shared responsibilities.
questions.subStrandTitle: Family as a Place of Learning
questions.learningOutcome: Identify ways families transmit religious values and responsible conduct.

questions.prompt: Which action shows respect for elders in many religious and cultural communities?
options: Listening politely and offering help when needed
Ignoring all guidance from older people
Speaking rudely to gain attention
Refusing every family duty
questions.correctAnswer: Listening politely and offering help when needed
questions.explanation: Respect for elders is shown through courtesy, listening, service, and appreciation of their guidance.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize respectful behaviour toward parents, guardians, elders, and leaders.

questions.prompt: What is servant leadership?
options: Leading by serving others responsibly and fairly
Using power to threaten people
Avoiding all duties as a leader
Taking credit for other people's work
questions.correctAnswer: Leading by serving others responsibly and fairly
questions.explanation: Servant leadership focuses on service, humility, responsibility, and the wellbeing of the community.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the meaning of servant leadership in religious and community life.

questions.prompt: Which quality should a religious youth leader show when resolving a disagreement?
options: Fairness
Favouritism
Anger
Dishonesty
questions.correctAnswer: Fairness
questions.explanation: Fairness helps a leader listen to all sides and seek a just solution.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify qualities of responsible leaders in religious and community settings.

questions.prompt: Why is cooperation important in a faith-based community project?
options: It helps people combine abilities and serve the community better
It allows one person to control all decisions
It prevents learners from sharing ideas
It makes accountability unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: It helps people combine abilities and serve the community better
questions.explanation: Cooperation improves service because members contribute different gifts, time, and ideas toward a shared goal.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how cooperation strengthens community service.

questions.prompt: A learner is given money to buy items for a charity visit. Which action shows accountability?
options: Keeping receipts and reporting how the money was used
Spending some money secretly
Guessing the cost without records
Blaming others for missing funds
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping receipts and reporting how the money was used
questions.explanation: Accountability means being answerable for resources and duties in an honest and transparent way.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply accountability when handling responsibilities and shared resources.

questions.prompt: Which response best shows respect when a parent or guardian corrects a learner?
options: Listen, reflect, and ask for guidance on how to improve
Shout back before understanding the concern
Tell lies to avoid responsibility
Repeat the mistake to annoy the family
questions.correctAnswer: Listen, reflect, and ask for guidance on how to improve
questions.explanation: Respectful correction involves listening, self-control, honesty, and willingness to change.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply religious values when receiving correction at home or school.

questions.prompt: A youth group has members from different religions. Which leadership approach would best promote unity?
options: Allow fair participation and focus on shared service values
Give duties only to one faith group
Make jokes about minority beliefs
Cancel all projects because members differ
questions.correctAnswer: Allow fair participation and focus on shared service values
questions.explanation: Inclusive leadership respects diversity and builds cooperation around shared values and goals.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply inclusive leadership in religiously diverse groups.

questions.prompt: Which decision best balances obedience and moral responsibility?
options: Respect a leader but refuse instructions that harm others or require dishonesty
Obey any instruction even if it is harmful
Reject every instruction from a leader
Follow friends only when they break rules
questions.correctAnswer: Respect a leader but refuse instructions that harm others or require dishonesty
questions.explanation: Religious values encourage respect for authority, but they also require conscience, truth, and protection of human dignity.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze situations where obedience must be guided by conscience and moral values.

questions.prompt: Which plan best shows responsible leadership for a religious youth club outreach?
options: Set clear goals, assign duties fairly, track resources, and review results
Let one person decide everything without records
Start collecting items without permission
Choose duties based on favouritism
questions.correctAnswer: Set clear goals, assign duties fairly, track resources, and review results
questions.explanation: A responsible plan combines service, fairness, accountability, and reflection after the activity.
questions.learningOutcome: Create responsible plans for faith-inspired community service.

questions.prompt: What does stewardship mean in religious education?
options: Responsible care for people, resources, talents, and creation
Using resources carelessly
Owning everything without responsibility
Avoiding all service to others
questions.correctAnswer: Responsible care for people, resources, talents, and creation
questions.explanation: Stewardship teaches that resources and abilities should be used responsibly for the wellbeing of people and creation.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the meaning of stewardship in religious and moral life.

questions.prompt: Which school action best shows care for creation?
options: Saving water and planting trees with a care schedule
Leaving taps running after use
Burning plastic near classrooms
Throwing litter into drainage channels
questions.correctAnswer: Saving water and planting trees with a care schedule
questions.explanation: Care for creation includes practical actions that protect water, soil, air, plants, animals, and people.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify actions that demonstrate care for the environment.

questions.prompt: Which value is shown when learners share extra food with a classmate who lacks lunch?
options: Generosity
Wastefulness
Pride
Neglect
questions.correctAnswer: Generosity
questions.explanation: Generosity is the willingness to share resources with others, especially when someone is in need.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize values shown through responsible sharing of resources.

questions.prompt: Why do many religious teachings encourage people to protect water sources?
options: Water supports life and should be used responsibly
Water should be wasted to show wealth
Water pollution helps communities grow
Clean water matters only to farmers
questions.correctAnswer: Water supports life and should be used responsibly
questions.explanation: Protecting water sources shows respect for life, health, and the needs of present and future communities.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why religious values support responsible care for water resources.

questions.prompt: A learner has talent in music. Which use of the talent best reflects stewardship?
options: Composing a song that promotes peace and respect
Using music to insult another group
Refusing to practise but demanding praise
Disrupting worship or assembly for attention
questions.correctAnswer: Composing a song that promotes peace and respect
questions.explanation: Talents are used responsibly when they build others up and support positive values.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply stewardship values to personal gifts and abilities.

questions.prompt: Which choice best shows stewardship of time?
options: Balancing worship, study, rest, service, and family duties
Spending all study time on gossip
Ignoring every responsibility until the last minute
Using prayer as an excuse to avoid helping at home
questions.correctAnswer: Balancing worship, study, rest, service, and family duties
questions.explanation: Responsible time use includes planning duties, learning, service, worship, and healthy rest.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply stewardship to time management and personal responsibilities.

questions.prompt: How can a religious club make a food donation drive accountable?
options: Record donations, store items safely, and distribute them through trusted adults
Hide some items for leaders
Guess the number of items without checking
Give donations only to friends of the leaders
questions.correctAnswer: Record donations, store items safely, and distribute them through trusted adults
questions.explanation: Accountability protects trust by tracking resources and ensuring they reach the intended people fairly.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply accountability to projects that use shared resources.

questions.prompt: A school clean-up day collects many plastic bottles. Which next step best shows environmental stewardship?
options: Sort the waste and send recyclable items to a proper collection point
Burn the bottles beside the classroom
Throw the bottles into a stream
Leave the bottles behind the kitchen
questions.correctAnswer: Sort the waste and send recyclable items to a proper collection point
questions.explanation: Sorting and recycling reduce pollution and protect health and the environment.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose responsible waste management practices that protect people and creation.

questions.prompt: Which question best helps evaluate whether an environmental project reflects religious values?
options: Does it protect life, promote responsibility, and involve the community fairly?
Does it make one person look important?
Can it hide pollution from visitors?
Does it avoid all planning and records?
questions.correctAnswer: Does it protect life, promote responsibility, and involve the community fairly?
questions.explanation: A values-based evaluation checks care for life, responsible use of resources, fairness, and community participation.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze stewardship projects using religious and moral values.

questions.prompt: A class planted seedlings, but half dried up. Which response best shows responsible stewardship?
options: Find the cause and create a watering and protection timetable
Blame one learner without checking facts
Stop caring for the remaining seedlings
Plant more trees without changing the plan
questions.correctAnswer: Find the cause and create a watering and protection timetable
questions.explanation: Responsible stewardship includes reflection, planning, and correcting what failed.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze project outcomes and improve environmental care plans.

questions.prompt: Which one-month school stewardship plan is strongest?
options: Assign teams for water saving, tree care, waste sorting, and weekly review
Hold one speech and take no action
Punish questions about the plan
Collect money without recording it
questions.correctAnswer: Assign teams for water saving, tree care, waste sorting, and weekly review
questions.explanation: A strong plan has clear duties, accountability, practical action, and regular review.
questions.learningOutcome: Create practical stewardship plans for school and community settings.

questions.prompt: What is peacebuilding?
options: Actions that prevent conflict and restore healthy relationships
A way of spreading rumours
A competition to embarrass opponents
A method of avoiding all communication
questions.correctAnswer: Actions that prevent conflict and restore healthy relationships
questions.explanation: Peacebuilding uses truth, listening, justice, forgiveness, and cooperation to reduce conflict and repair relationships.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the meaning of peacebuilding in religious and community life.

questions.prompt: Which value is most needed when two learners want a fair solution after conflict?
options: Justice
Revenge
Mockery
Favouritism
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Justice seeks fairness, truth, responsibility, and repair rather than revenge.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify values that support fair conflict resolution.

questions.prompt: Which action is most likely to reduce conflict in a class group?
options: Listening to each side before agreeing on a fair way forward
Allowing rumours to spread
Ignoring the affected learners
Encouraging one side to revenge
questions.correctAnswer: Listening to each side before agreeing on a fair way forward
questions.explanation: Listening helps people understand the issue and work toward a fair, peaceful solution.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply listening and fairness in resolving disagreements.

questions.prompt: Why should forgiveness be joined with responsibility after wrongdoing?
options: Because peace is stronger when harm is acknowledged and repaired
Because forgiveness means ignoring all harm
Because responsibility prevents apology
Because repair is never part of justice
questions.correctAnswer: Because peace is stronger when harm is acknowledged and repaired
questions.explanation: Forgiveness supports peace, while responsibility and repair help restore trust and protect justice.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how forgiveness, responsibility, and justice work together.

questions.prompt: A learner damages another learner's book and apologises. Which response best balances forgiveness and justice?
options: Accept the apology while agreeing on repair or replacement
Demand revenge beyond the damage caused
Pretend no harm occurred and learn nothing
Refuse any discussion with a teacher
questions.correctAnswer: Accept the apology while agreeing on repair or replacement
questions.explanation: Forgiveness can restore relationships, while repair addresses responsibility for the damage.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply restorative approaches to everyday conflicts.

questions.prompt: Which approach best prevents religious misunderstanding in school?
options: Encourage respectful questions and accurate information from trusted sources
Reward learners for mocking unfamiliar beliefs
Forbid all learners from explaining their traditions
Let rumours guide class discussions
questions.correctAnswer: Encourage respectful questions and accurate information from trusted sources
questions.explanation: Accurate information and respectful conversation reduce suspicion and support peaceful coexistence.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply respectful communication to prevent religious misunderstanding.

questions.prompt: Which question best tests whether a peace agreement is fair?
options: Does it listen to affected people and address the real cause of harm?
Does it silence the weakest person?
Does it hide all facts from the group?
Does it reward wrongdoing without repair?
questions.correctAnswer: Does it listen to affected people and address the real cause of harm?
questions.explanation: A fair agreement considers truth, affected people, causes, responsibility, and practical repair.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze peace agreements using fairness, truth, and responsibility.

questions.prompt: A conflict started because one group was excluded from planning a school event. Which solution best reflects justice?
options: Include representatives from all affected groups and agree on fair duties
Let only the loudest group decide
Cancel the event without discussion
Punish the excluded group for complaining
questions.correctAnswer: Include representatives from all affected groups and agree on fair duties
questions.explanation: Justice requires fair participation, listening, and shared responsibility in decisions that affect people.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze how inclusion and fairness can reduce conflict.

questions.prompt: Which peace week activity would best connect religious values with action?
options: Dialogue circles, service tasks, anti-bullying messages, and reflection on shared values
A contest to shame learners who disagree
A rule that only one group may speak
A campaign encouraging insults online
questions.correctAnswer: Dialogue circles, service tasks, anti-bullying messages, and reflection on shared values
questions.explanation: A strong peace activity combines respectful conversation, service, responsible speech, and shared values.
questions.learningOutcome: Create peacebuilding activities rooted in religious and moral values.

questions.prompt: What is charity in religious and moral life?
options: Loving service and support given to people in need
Taking resources from vulnerable people
Helping only when praise is guaranteed
Ignoring people who face difficulty
questions.correctAnswer: Loving service and support given to people in need
questions.explanation: Charity expresses compassion through practical help that respects the dignity of others.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe charity as a form of religious and moral service.

questions.prompt: In Islam, which practice involves required giving to support those in need?
options: Zakat
Salah
Hajj
Tawhid
questions.correctAnswer: Zakat
questions.explanation: Zakat is required giving that promotes social responsibility and care for vulnerable people.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify examples of religious giving and service.

questions.prompt: Which action best shows service in a school community?
options: Helping clean a shared space without expecting special treatment
Leaving duties for younger learners only
Taking credit for another person's work
Refusing to help unless paid
questions.correctAnswer: Helping clean a shared space without expecting special treatment
questions.explanation: Service is shown through useful action done with humility, responsibility, and concern for others.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize practical examples of service in school life.

questions.prompt: Why should service protect the dignity of the people being helped?
options: Because every person deserves respect, privacy, and fair treatment
Because help is useful only when people are embarrassed
Because dignity matters only to wealthy people
Because service should make helpers look superior
questions.correctAnswer: Because every person deserves respect, privacy, and fair treatment
questions.explanation: Religious values teach that help should respect the worth and privacy of the person receiving support.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why dignity and respect are important in service activities.

questions.prompt: Which choice best shows responsible giving?
options: Giving useful items in good condition through a trusted process
Giving broken items to avoid disposing of them
Announcing private details about people receiving help
Keeping donated items for personal use
questions.correctAnswer: Giving useful items in good condition through a trusted process
questions.explanation: Responsible giving considers real needs, quality, accountability, and the dignity of recipients.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply religious values to responsible giving and support for others.

questions.prompt: A learner notices a new classmate sitting alone every break. Which response best reflects compassion?
options: Invite the classmate into a respectful activity and listen kindly
Laugh at the classmate for being alone
Ignore the classmate to avoid responsibility
Share rumours about the classmate
questions.correctAnswer: Invite the classmate into a respectful activity and listen kindly
questions.explanation: Compassion notices another person's need and responds with kindness and inclusion.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply compassion to everyday relationships in school.

questions.prompt: Which step should come before a class begins a community service project?
options: Identify a real need with guidance from responsible adults
Collect money without a plan
Choose a project only because it is easy to photograph
Promise help before asking what is needed
questions.correctAnswer: Identify a real need with guidance from responsible adults
questions.explanation: Good service starts by understanding actual needs and planning with trusted guidance.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan service projects that respond to real community needs.

questions.prompt: Which reflection question would best help learners improve after a service activity?
options: What did we learn, who benefited, and what should we improve next time?
How can we make ourselves famous?
Who can we blame for every difficulty?
How can we avoid serving again?
questions.correctAnswer: What did we learn, who benefited, and what should we improve next time?
questions.explanation: Reflection helps learners connect service with values, impact, accountability, and future improvement.
questions.learningOutcome: Reflect on service experiences to improve future action.

questions.prompt: A service project helps some learners but embarrasses them publicly. What is the main ethical problem?
options: The project does not protect dignity and privacy
The project has too many useful items
The project includes too much kindness
The project avoids all publicity
questions.correctAnswer: The project does not protect dignity and privacy
questions.explanation: Service should meet needs without shaming people or exposing private struggles unnecessarily.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze service activities for dignity, privacy, and fairness.

questions.prompt: Which service plan best shows both compassion and accountability?
options: Confirm the need, assign duties, keep records, serve respectfully, and review results
Collect supplies secretly and distribute them without permission
Give items only to friends
Avoid records so nobody asks questions
questions.correctAnswer: Confirm the need, assign duties, keep records, serve respectfully, and review results
questions.explanation: Strong service joins kindness with planning, transparency, dignity, and reflection.
questions.learningOutcome: Create service plans that combine compassion, dignity, and accountability.

questions.prompt: What is cyberbullying?
options: Using digital tools to threaten, shame, or harass another person
Reading a school notice online
Submitting homework through a learning platform
Joining a respectful class discussion
questions.correctAnswer: Using digital tools to threaten, shame, or harass another person
questions.explanation: Cyberbullying misuses digital spaces to harm dignity, peace, and emotional safety.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify harmful digital behaviour and its moral effects.

questions.prompt: Which online action best reflects religious values of truth and respect?
options: Verify information before sharing and avoid insulting comments
Forward rumours to become popular
Use anonymous accounts to mock classmates
Share private photos without permission
questions.correctAnswer: Verify information before sharing and avoid insulting comments
questions.explanation: Responsible digital conduct protects truth, dignity, privacy, and peace.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply religious values to responsible use of digital media.

questions.prompt: Which example shows discrimination based on religion?
options: Refusing to include a learner in a group because of their faith
Sharing class notes with everyone
Asking a respectful question about a festival
Working together on a clean-up project
questions.correctAnswer: Refusing to include a learner in a group because of their faith
questions.explanation: Discrimination treats a person unfairly because of identity or belief and harms dignity.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize discrimination and choose inclusive actions.

questions.prompt: Why is privacy important when using digital media?
options: It protects people's dignity, safety, and personal information
It allows rumours to spread faster
It makes honesty unnecessary online
It helps people embarrass others secretly
questions.correctAnswer: It protects people's dignity, safety, and personal information
questions.explanation: Respecting privacy is part of treating people with dignity and avoiding harm.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why privacy is a moral responsibility in digital spaces.

questions.prompt: A class chat starts insulting a learner's religion. What should a responsible learner do?
options: Refuse to join, save evidence if needed, and report to a trusted adult
Add more insults to look brave
Forward the messages to more groups
Tell the targeted learner to stay silent forever
questions.correctAnswer: Refuse to join, save evidence if needed, and report to a trusted adult
questions.explanation: Responsible action protects the targeted learner and helps stop harmful digital behaviour.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe and responsible responses to online harassment.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes religious freedom in a school community?
options: People should be treated with dignity while practising their faith responsibly
One learner may force everyone to copy their worship
People may insult any religion without consequence
Faith differences should be used to deny friendship
questions.correctAnswer: People should be treated with dignity while practising their faith responsibly
questions.explanation: Religious freedom is linked with dignity, responsibility, respect for others, and peaceful coexistence.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain responsible respect for religious freedom in school life.

questions.prompt: Which online post best reflects moral courage?
options: A respectful message asking classmates to stop spreading a harmful rumour
A joke that targets another person's faith
A repost of private information without consent
A threat against someone who disagrees
questions.correctAnswer: A respectful message asking classmates to stop spreading a harmful rumour
questions.explanation: Moral courage can involve challenging harmful behaviour while still using respectful language.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply moral courage to digital communication.

questions.prompt: Which question best helps evaluate whether a social media message should be shared?
options: Is it true, respectful, necessary, and safe to share?
Will it embarrass someone quickly?
Can it make me popular even if false?
Will it start conflict between groups?
questions.correctAnswer: Is it true, respectful, necessary, and safe to share?
questions.explanation: A responsible learner checks truth, respect, purpose, and possible harm before sharing digital content.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze digital messages using religious values and responsible citizenship.

questions.prompt: A school wants rules for respectful online learning. Which rule is strongest?
options: Use truthful words, protect privacy, report harm, and disagree respectfully
Post private images whenever classmates annoy you
Forward any message before checking it
Allow insults if they are called jokes
questions.correctAnswer: Use truthful words, protect privacy, report harm, and disagree respectfully
questions.explanation: Strong digital rules protect truth, dignity, privacy, safety, and peaceful communication.
questions.learningOutcome: Create digital conduct guidelines based on religious and moral values.

questions.prompt: What is self-control?
options: The ability to manage feelings, words, and actions responsibly
Doing anything one wants immediately
Blaming others for every mistake
Avoiding all advice from adults
questions.correctAnswer: The ability to manage feelings, words, and actions responsibly
questions.explanation: Self-control helps a learner pause, think, and choose actions that respect values and other people.
questions.strandTitle: Personal Growth and Moral Decision Making
questions.learningOutcome: Describe self-control as a value for responsible living.

questions.prompt: Which action best shows gratitude?
options: Thanking people and using their support responsibly
Complaining about every act of kindness
Hiding help from others to avoid appreciation
Taking gifts as if they are deserved
questions.correctAnswer: Thanking people and using their support responsibly
questions.explanation: Gratitude recognizes kindness and responds with appreciation and responsible use of what is received.
questions.strandTitle: Personal Growth and Moral Decision Making
questions.learningOutcome: Identify actions that show gratitude in daily life.

questions.prompt: Why is repentance important after wrongdoing?
options: It involves admitting wrong, seeking forgiveness, and changing behaviour
It means blaming the victim
It removes the need to repair harm
It allows a person to repeat the same mistake proudly
questions.correctAnswer: It involves admitting wrong, seeking forgiveness, and changing behaviour
questions.explanation: Repentance includes honesty about wrongdoing and a sincere effort to turn toward better conduct.
questions.strandTitle: Personal Growth and Moral Decision Making
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of repentance in moral growth.

questions.prompt: Which choice best shows resilience guided by faith and values?
options: Seeking support, learning from failure, and continuing to do what is right
Giving up every duty after one mistake
Hiding problems through dishonesty
Hurting others because one feels disappointed
questions.correctAnswer: Seeking support, learning from failure, and continuing to do what is right
questions.explanation: Resilience helps a learner recover from difficulty while staying committed to responsible choices.
questions.strandTitle: Personal Growth and Moral Decision Making
questions.learningOutcome: Apply resilience when facing challenges and moral pressure.

questions.prompt: A learner is angry after being corrected. Which response best shows self-control?
options: Pause, listen, and respond respectfully after calming down
Shout insults immediately
Walk away and spread rumours
Break another learner's property
questions.correctAnswer: Pause, listen, and respond respectfully after calming down
questions.explanation: Self-control gives time to choose respectful words and avoid harmful reactions.
questions.strandTitle: Personal Growth and Moral Decision Making
questions.learningOutcome: Apply self-control in emotionally difficult situations.

questions.prompt: Which habit best supports spiritual and moral growth?
options: Regular reflection on actions and willingness to improve
Avoiding all feedback
Repeating mistakes without concern
Judging others without self-examination
questions.correctAnswer: Regular reflection on actions and willingness to improve
questions.explanation: Reflection helps learners connect beliefs, values, behaviour, and personal improvement.
questions.strandTitle: Personal Growth and Moral Decision Making
questions.learningOutcome: Use reflection to support spiritual and moral growth.

questions.prompt: Which decision-making step should come before acting in a difficult moral situation?
options: Consider the facts, values involved, consequences, and trusted guidance
Do what the loudest friend suggests
Choose the easiest action without thinking
Hide the situation from every responsible adult
questions.correctAnswer: Consider the facts, values involved, consequences, and trusted guidance
questions.explanation: Wise decisions require facts, values, consequences, conscience, and guidance where needed.
questions.strandTitle: Personal Growth and Moral Decision Making
questions.learningOutcome: Apply a responsible process when making moral decisions.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to apologize after spreading a false story. Which apology is most complete?
options: Admit the lie, apologize, correct the false story, and avoid repeating it
Say sorry but continue spreading the story
Blame everyone else for believing it
Apologize only if a teacher is watching
questions.correctAnswer: Admit the lie, apologize, correct the false story, and avoid repeating it
questions.explanation: A complete apology includes truth, remorse, repair, and a change in behaviour.
questions.strandTitle: Personal Growth and Moral Decision Making
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze actions needed to restore trust after wrongdoing.

questions.prompt: Which plan best helps a learner resist repeated pressure to join cheating?
options: Prepare a firm response, sit away from pressure, seek support, and study honestly
Promise to cheat only once
Avoid studying and depend on classmates
Blame the teacher for setting tests
questions.correctAnswer: Prepare a firm response, sit away from pressure, seek support, and study honestly
questions.explanation: A practical plan combines moral courage, boundaries, support, and responsible preparation.
questions.strandTitle: Personal Growth and Moral Decision Making
questions.learningOutcome: Create strategies for resisting peer pressure and choosing honest conduct.

questions.prompt: Which action best supports a grieving classmate?
options: Listen kindly and connect the classmate with trusted support
Tell the classmate to stop feeling sad immediately
Share the classmate's story without permission
Avoid the classmate until they seem cheerful
questions.correctAnswer: Listen kindly and connect the classmate with trusted support
questions.explanation: Compassionate support respects feelings, privacy, and the need for guidance from trusted people.
questions.strandTitle: Personal Growth and Moral Decision Making
questions.learningOutcome: Apply compassion when supporting people facing grief or difficulty.

questions.prompt: Which description best defines interfaith dialogue?
options: Respectful conversation among people of different faiths to build understanding
A debate meant to humiliate another religion
A rule that no one may explain their beliefs
A way to spread rumours about worship practices
questions.correctAnswer: Respectful conversation among people of different faiths to build understanding
questions.explanation: Interfaith dialogue encourages listening, accurate understanding, and peaceful relationships among communities.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe interfaith dialogue as a way of promoting understanding and peace.

questions.prompt: Which value best supports national cohesion in a religiously diverse country?
options: Respect
Hatred
Mockery
Exclusion
questions.correctAnswer: Respect
questions.explanation: Respect helps citizens live peacefully with people whose backgrounds and beliefs differ from theirs.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify values that support national cohesion and peaceful coexistence.

questions.prompt: Which action would best promote inclusion during a school cultural and religious day?
options: Allow groups to share approved presentations respectfully and safely
Invite only one group and exclude the rest
Permit jokes that insult minority traditions
Cancel questions from learners who want to understand
questions.correctAnswer: Allow groups to share approved presentations respectfully and safely
questions.explanation: Inclusive events provide fair opportunities for learning while maintaining respect and safety.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply inclusive practices in school activities involving different faiths.

questions.prompt: Why should stereotypes about religious communities be avoided?
options: They can spread false ideas and lead to unfair treatment
They always help people understand accurately
They are the best source for learning
They make respectful dialogue unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: They can spread false ideas and lead to unfair treatment
questions.explanation: Stereotypes reduce people to unfair labels and can damage trust, dignity, and peace.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why stereotypes harm interfaith relations and social cohesion.

questions.prompt: A rumour is causing tension between two faith clubs. Which step is most ethical?
options: Check facts with responsible leaders before making accusations
Punish one club without listening
Share the rumour more widely
Let anger decide what happened
questions.correctAnswer: Check facts with responsible leaders before making accusations
questions.explanation: Ethical investigation protects truth, fairness, and the dignity of all people involved.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply truthfulness and fairness to prevent interfaith conflict.

questions.prompt: Which shared activity is most likely to strengthen friendship between different faith groups?
options: A community clean-up followed by respectful reflection on shared values
A contest to prove one group is superior
A campaign to avoid all contact
A meeting where only one group may speak
questions.correctAnswer: A community clean-up followed by respectful reflection on shared values
questions.explanation: Shared service allows groups to cooperate around common values such as care, responsibility, and peace.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply shared service as a way of building interfaith understanding.

questions.prompt: Which question best evaluates whether an interfaith event was successful?
options: Did participants learn accurately, feel respected, and agree on positive next steps?
Did one group silence everyone else?
Did the event create new rumours?
Did learners leave with more stereotypes?
questions.correctAnswer: Did participants learn accurately, feel respected, and agree on positive next steps?
questions.explanation: A successful interfaith event should build knowledge, respect, trust, and practical cooperation.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze interfaith activities using respect, accuracy, and cooperation.

questions.prompt: Which response best protects freedom of worship and classroom order?
options: Allow respectful religious expression while following school rules and respecting others
Allow one learner to disrupt everyone else
Ban all respectful mention of religion
Let learners insult beliefs they dislike
questions.correctAnswer: Allow respectful religious expression while following school rules and respecting others
questions.explanation: Freedom of worship works with responsibility, respect, and agreed rules for a peaceful school community.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze how religious freedom and responsibility can support peaceful coexistence.

questions.prompt: Which plan best prepares learners for a respectful visit to different places of worship?
options: Learn expected conduct, seek permission, prepare questions, and reflect on shared values
Arrive without permission and interrupt worship
Touch sacred objects to test reactions
Write jokes about every unfamiliar practice
questions.correctAnswer: Learn expected conduct, seek permission, prepare questions, and reflect on shared values
questions.explanation: Preparation helps learners observe respectfully, ask informed questions, and connect learning with values.
questions.learningOutcome: Create respectful plans for learning from different places of worship.

questions.prompt: A Grade 8 class wants to promote unity in the school. Which campaign best reflects Religious Education values?
options: A campaign on respect, truthful speech, shared service, and peaceful conflict resolution
A campaign ranking religions from best to worst
A campaign encouraging learners to avoid those with different beliefs
A campaign spreading jokes about worship practices
questions.correctAnswer: A campaign on respect, truthful speech, shared service, and peaceful conflict resolution
questions.explanation: Religious Education values support unity through respect, truth, service, justice, and peace.
questions.learningOutcome: Create school campaigns that promote unity through religious and moral values.
